validity.researcher_notes: The row exists and is correctly classified: this is Kinder Morgan/NGPL's 'Gulf Coast Southbound Project (Phase II)', a compression-only expansion (five existing compressor stations in Victoria, Wharton, Harrison, Angelina and Cass Counties, Texas) that raised southbound firm capacity on NGPL's Gulf Coast Mainline System by 300,000 Dth/d (~300 MMcf/d) to serve Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction facility in San Patricio County, Texas. Sources: FERC Federal Register Notice of Application, Docket CP19-99-000 (2019-03-14, filed by Natural Gas Pipeline Co. of America); EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, 'Historical Projects' tab, row 'NGPL Gulf Coast Southbound Project (Phase II)' (Beg_State IL, End_State TX, Completed 2021-03-01); Kinder Morgan's own Q3-2020 earnings release (via BOE Report, Oct. 21 2020) naming the delivery point as 'Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction facility in San Patricio County, Texas.' All three independently place the destination facilities in Texas. The sheet's EndState/Province = 'Louisiana' is wrong (the sheet's own EndPrefecture/District = 'Agua Dulce Hub' is itself a well-documented South Texas gas hub near Corpus Christi — this looks like the same defect flagged on sibling row P2039 Phase I, which has the identical Louisiana/Texas mismatch). Note the harvested wiki citation for RBN Energy also mis-tags the destination 'LA' — so GEM likely inherited the error from that page rather than from an EIA/FERC source, which both say Texas. StartLocation/StartState (Chicago, Illinois) are correct and independently confirmed (EIA Beg_State = IL; RBN Origin = Chicago Market, IL).

validity.recommendation: Consider updating SegmentCost to a later-stage figure (KM's own $203M in-progress estimate, or EIA's $176M post-completion figure) rather than the 2019 pre-filing estimate — flagging for a judgment call, not overriding.
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded SegmentCost (145,000,000 USD) matches, within rounding, the ORIGINAL March 2019 FERC application's cost estimate of $145,248,818 (Federal Register Notice of Application, Docket CP19-99-000) — so the current value is sourced and I am staging that as the replacement ref for the dead eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php# link. But two LATER, independent sources give materially higher figures for the same project as it proceeded: Kinder Morgan's own Q3 2020 earnings release (BOE Report, Oct. 21 2020) states 'The approximately $203 million project (KMI's share: $101.5 million)' while construction was still underway, and the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook's post-completion 'Historical Projects' record lists Cost (millions) = 176 for the same project. $145M (2019 filing) -> $203M (KM, in-progress, Oct 2020) -> $176M (EIA, post-completion) is a real spread (both later figures are >20% off the filed estimate, in different directions from the filing and from each other), consistent with a project whose scope/cost was revised during construction and then reconciled at completion. I did not find a document reconciling all three, so I am not overriding GEM's recorded value (it does match its own cited-era source), but flagging that a $145M SegmentCost reflects the 2019 pre-construction filing, not the as-built cost — a researcher should decide whether GEM's cost convention wants the filed estimate or the completed actual cost, and if the latter, EIA's $176M (the only post-completion, non-operator-sourced figure) is the better candidate.
